target_customer: Tire shops, dealers, and fleet service centers that install tires
problem: Tire changing is slow, labor intensive and hard to staff; RoboTire built a robot that could change a set of four tires in about 10 minutes.
business_model: Hardware robot licensed to service centers and dealers, with per-tire pricing in pilots

founders.name: Victor Darolfi
previous_startups: Serial entrepreneur with one exit per YC bio
founders.background_notes: YC bio cites 11 years of robotics and automation equipment experience with installs at Tesla, SpaceX, Zume Pizza, Space Systems Loral, Zee Aero, Intel and Lam Research. TechCrunch (2020) says he planned to manufacture in his hometown, Detroit.

founders.name: Will Mapes
founders.background_notes: Listed under Former Founders on the YC page with no bio.

exit.reason: Filed for Chapter 7 liquidation on January 19, 2024 in Delaware; the filing coverage does not state a cause

technical_complexity.rationale: Machine vision, lug nut removal and wheel handling across many vehicles required robotics and hardware work; a TechCrunch piece in 2020 notes a $250,000 system and robot partners.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware with licensed installs in shops could lock in customers, but the system was unproven at scale and later critics questioned its speed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Discount Tire's parent led the 2021 Series A and hosted the first install in 2022, then became the largest creditor in the 2024 bankruptcy.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (February 2020) says a human mechanic needs about an hour for four tires; the pilot pricing was $5 to $7 per tire; labor shortages in shops were later cited by press.

branding.domain_note: Used robotire.com; the site did not load from this research environment.
branding.brand_signature: The robot itself: viral videos of it changing tires
branding.community_and_virality: A TikTok clip by a tire wholesaler had over 229,000 views per the Daily Dot; Dallas News and other outlets covered installs in 2022 and 2023.

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive, memorable name and a visual product that drew viral video and trade press, though it did not translate into sustained revenue.

outcome_analysis: RoboTire raised small early rounds and a $7.5M Series A in October 2021 led by Discount Tire, installed its first system in 2022, then filed Chapter 7 in January 2024 with about $12.7M in liabilities and Discount Tire as the largest creditor. The sourced pattern is a capital-intensive hardware company that ran out of money after one large round and was reportedly seeking more investors; the filing coverage states no cause.
notes: The pre-seed and seed come from one outlet (TechCrunch, February 2020); the seed is described as closed before YC with no exact date. An aggregator lists a $150,000 pre-seed from YC, unverified and not recorded. The Robot Report says the Series A was in 2022 while TechCrunch dated it October 2021; TechCrunch is used. No total raised was found. The Truth About Cars (January 24, 2024) reports $12.7M liabilities, a $1.6M secured claim and a separate $3.3M claim by Discount Tire, and says the company was reportedly seeking more investors; it also questions the robot's speed. Competitor list is empty: the February 2020 TechCrunch piece names no robotic tire-change rivals (human mechanics are the incumbent), and rivals found by search (PitPro, Automated Tire) emerged in 2026. Founder education not found. The YC page lists the company under Former Founders with no status; the directory status is Inactive.
